title: Sunny and the Warm Rock | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka finds a large smooth rock that has held the warmth of the whole day inside it, and sits against it as the cool night air flows past, feeling perfectly held. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The rock was warm.

Sunny pressed her paw flat against it and felt the warmth come through immediately — not sharp or hot, but deep and steady and slow. The rock had been gathering heat from the sun all day and now, in the middle of the night, it was giving it away. Quietly. Without being asked.

She leaned her whole side against it.

The warmth spread through her fur and into her skin. The cool night air was moving past, but here — pressed against the rock — she was warm all down one side.

She pressed harder.

The rock was enormous. Much bigger than her. It had been sitting in the same place for longer than she could imagine. Long before there were quokkas walking past on moonlit nights. Long before the bush around her had been the bush it was. Just a rock, holding its place, storing the heat of every single day.

She thought: the rock just does its job, every day, without making a fuss about it.

She sat all the way down and let the warmth come through her back.

The night air was cool on her face.

The rock was warm on her back.

These were two very good things to have at once.

She closed her eyes.

The rock gave her its stored-up warmth, patient and slow and steady.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, warm rock. Goodnight, little one.
